## Remarks

The first diagram displays the open deformation family $D_i=M\setminus B$,
with structure map $p$ induced by $M\to\mathbb P^1$. Both squares are
Cartesian: $j$ includes the special fibre, while $u$ includes the complement
of that fibre. Here $\mathbb A^1=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{\infty\}$; the local
parameter $t$ used above vanishes at $\infty$, not at the origin of this
ordinary-fibre chart.

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large, row sep=large, font=\Large, labels={font=\large}]
C_XY \arrow[r, hook, "j"] \arrow[d] & D_i \arrow[d, "p"] & Y\times\mathbb A^1 \arrow[l, hook', "u"'] \arrow[d] \\
\{\infty\} \arrow[r, hook] & \mathbb P^1 & \mathbb A^1 \arrow[l, hook']
\end{tikzcd}
```

For the full blowup family, write $E=\mathbb P(C_XY\oplus1)$ and
$W=\mathbb P(C_XY)$. Its infinity fibre is the divisor $B+E$, with each
summand occurring once. The second diagram shows the closed inclusions into
that fibre and their common boundary $W=B\cap E$. Removing $B$ leaves
$E\setminus W=C_XY$, the special fibre of $D_i$.

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large, row sep=large, font=\Large]
W \arrow[r, hook] \arrow[d, hook] & E \arrow[d, hook] \\
B \arrow[r, hook] & M_\infty
\end{tikzcd}
```

The projective completion $E$ is a projectivized cone in general; no regular
immersion is assumed in either diagram. Only under the regular-immersion
hypothesis stated above is $C_XY=N_{X/Y}$ a vector bundle. At the level of
cycles, flat pullback along $Y\times\mathbb A^1\to Y$ raises dimension from
$m$ to $m+1$; localization lifts this class to $A_{m+1}(D_i)$ and $j^!$
lowers dimension to $m$, yielding the stated $\sigma_i$. The chart and
localization arguments above establish these facts independently of the
figures.

## Remarks

The right-hand square displays the middle matching in the source-first order.
Here $v'(x_i,x_j,x_k)=(x_i,x_j)$, $u'(x_i,x_j,x_k)=(x_j,x_k)$,
$u(x_i,x_j)=x_j$, $v(x_j,x_k)=x_j$, and $h(x_i,x_j,x_k)=(x_i,x_k)$.
Thus $uv'=vu'$ and $T_{ijk}=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$; the arrow $h$ is
proper by the base-change description in the definition.

```tikzcd
[font=\LARGE, every label/.append style={font=\Large}, column sep=large, row sep=large]
Z_{ik} & T_{ijk} \arrow[l, "h"'] \arrow[r, "v'"] \arrow[d, "u'"'] & Z_{ij} \arrow[d, "u"] \\
& Z_{jk} \arrow[r, "v"'] & X_j
```

The same matching gives the following order of operations on Borel–Moore classes:

```tikzcd
[font=\LARGE, every label/.append style={font=\Large}, column sep=large, row sep=large]
H_{p+q}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij}\times Z_{jk})
\arrow[r, "\Delta_{X_j}^{!}"] &
H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(T_{ijk})
\arrow[r, "h_*"] &
H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik})
```

The input is $a\boxtimes b$, with ordered coordinates $(i,j,j,k)$.
The first arrow matches the middle pair using the positively complex-oriented
normal bundle $TX_j$ and lowers degree by $2d_j$; the second forgets the middle
point. The sheaf exchange for the right-hand square is precisely
$v'^*u^!\to u'^!v^*$, with no assertion that it is an isomorphism on arbitrary
supports. These diagrams only illustrate the definition; its well-formedness
and the cited compatibility proofs remain independent of the figures.

## Remarks

The supplied orientation makes both nonzero rows constant-coefficient rows.
On page $n+1$, the following schematic shows two columns of these rows;
all intermediate rows are zero. Here $a\geq0$ and the diagonal arrow has
bidegree $(n+1,-n)$.

```tikzcd
[font=\Large, labels={font=\large}, row sep=3em, column sep=4em]
E_{n+1}^{a,n}=H^a(B;R)u \arrow[dr, "d_{n+1}" description] & E_{n+1}^{a+n+1,n}=H^{a+n+1}(B;R)u \\
E_{n+1}^{a,0}=H^a(B;R) & E_{n+1}^{a+n+1,0}=H^{a+n+1}(B;R)
```

For $x\in H^a(B;R)$ the diagonal sends $xu$ to
$(-1)^a x\smile e(p)$; at $a=0$ it sends $u$ to $e(p)$.
Taking its cokernels in the bottom row and kernels in the top row gives the
two stable terms of proof step 3.1. Their short exact filtration sequence
then gives (1): $p^*$ factors through the bottom-row cokernel, while $p_!$
is the top-row quotient followed by its inclusion, using the orientation,
into $H^{k-n}(B;R)$. The cup maps in (1) retain its stated sign normalization.
The schematic neither asserts a splitting of the filtration nor identifies
$p_!$ with a cohomological axis edge; the proof above is independent of it.
